what: A GraphQL client sends queries to one endpoint and manages the answers in a cache. Components declare their data needs as fragments, the parent combines them into one query, and persisted queries send a short hash instead of the full text. Apollo Client, Relay and urql are the main choices.
like: Like a group lunch order: each person writes their own dish on a slip, the organiser staples them into one order for the restaurant, and everyone gets only their own plate.
why: Each component asks for exactly the fields it uses - no over-fetching
One request can fill a whole screen
Smaller, safer requests with persisted queries

steps.d: Each component declares a fragment next to its markup, e.g. AuthorDetails_author. It reads only those fields.
Fragments are spread into the parent and up to a route-level query. One network request covers the whole view.
The client looks in its normalized cache before the network; data that is already there renders immediately.
A chain of links adds auth headers, retries and persisted-query hashing before the HTTP call.

steps.t: Persisted queries shrink and secure it
steps.d: The client sends a SHA-256 hash; the server looks up the text. With GET, a CDN can cache it. An allowlist of persisted operations can also block unknown queries.

choices.d: Apollo Client is the general-purpose choice with a normalized cache. Relay is the most opinionated: compiler, strict fragment colocation and masking, built for large apps. urql is lighter and extensible, with an optional normalized cache (Graphcache).

Colocation keeps each component's data needs next to it. Masking hides fields a component did not ask for, so a child removing a field cannot silently break a parent. In Apollo enable it with dataMasking: true.
Automatic persisted queries cut request size and need no server setup. A registered allowlist (safelisting) also blocks unknown operations, which is a security gain.

choices.t: GraphQL or REST plus a query cache
choices.d: GraphQL pays off with many clients and screens needing different slices of a graph. For a few simple endpoints, REST with TanStack Query is lighter.

instead.why: REST or any fetch function with caching and no schema tooling
The cache design underneath Apollo and Relay, useful to explain on its own

breaks.d: Every field is requested at the top and passed down as props.
breaks.see: Slow responses and re-renders for unrelated changes
breaks.fix: Colocate fragments; split with deferred or lazy queries per section

breaks.d: Without masking, parents read child fields they never declared.
breaks.see: A harmless field removal breaks another component
breaks.fix: Turn on data masking; fragments per component

breaks.d: Mutation response omits fields or ids.
breaks.fix: Return the changed object with id and __typename; update list fields explicitly

say: Each component owns a fragment; the route composes them into one query, so the screen loads in a single request and nobody over-fetches.
I enable data masking so components only see what they asked for, which keeps refactors safe.
For production I use persisted queries - hashes instead of query text - with GET so a CDN can cache, and an allowlist so unknown queries are rejected.

followups.a: They let each component declare its own data, compose upward into one query, and avoid both over-fetching and tight coupling between parent and child.

followups.q: How do automatic persisted queries work?
followups.a: The client sends only a hash. If the server does not know it, it replies PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_FOUND and the client resends the hash with the full text; later requests use the hash alone.

followups.q: When is GraphQL the wrong call?
followups.a: When there are few endpoints and one client; the schema, tooling and cache complexity may not pay for themselves.

today: Apollo Client now offers data masking and fragment hooks such as useFragment, and GraphOS lets routers enforce a persisted-query allowlist, so type-safe fragment-first data loading is the mainstream pattern.

check.q: What is the main benefit of colocated fragments?
check.a: Each component states its own data needs, composed into one query
d: They remove the need for a schema
check.why: Colocation keeps requirements next to the UI and avoids over-fetching.

check.a: Hides fields a component did not request
check.why: It prevents hidden dependencies between parents and children.

check.q: What does the client send first with an automatic persisted query?
check.why: If the server lacks it, the client retries with the full text.
